title: Tokyo 1932: American State Department and Navy telegrams read by the Japanese Navy (米特情, Jan-Sept 1932), compared with FRUS

steps.what: Sixteen bundles inventoried (828 lines); bundles (1)-(8) transcribed image by image.
53 State Department telegrams found in FRUS and compared word by word with the Japanese copies: about 77 % of the words recovered (45-95 %); confidential passages unread.

Wrong readings share the true word's initial 63/137 (46 %) vs 6.3 % shuffled; truncations 95/119 (80 %) vs 6.1 %; p < 1e-4, 10,000 permutations; alphabetical-neighbour distance replicated on held-out batch d: compatible with a one-part code.
Kotani 2007 and Moriyama 2004/2007 mention the Japanese reading of State Department traffic (Gray; 1941); no publication of this file or of a comparison with FRUS found.

outcome.method_basis: The Japanese Navy's own recovered clear texts (1932), measured against the American text printed in FRUS.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Japanese reading rate on 53 telegrams compared with FRUS (four batches measured slightly differently).

validation.notes: No key recovered by us; the statistical test bears on the nature of the code (one-part), not on a key.

credits.note: file found, inventory, transcription of bundles (1)-(8), comparison with FRUS, one-part-code test

gaps.item: confidential (enciphered) passages, e.g. Grew no. 223 last 45 words, Johnson no. 1078 paras. 2-10: not read by the Japanese; text known from FRUS
code identification (Gray): needs the NARA RG 59 file copies with their groups
bundles (9)-(16): inventory only, not transcribed in full (JACAR images not redistributable)

texts.label: 米特情 copies, bundles (1)-(8), Jan-Apr 1932
texts.transcription_missing: No cipher groups survive: the Japanese copied only the clear text they had recovered.
texts.note: The decryption is the Japanese Navy's own recovered clear text of 1932, transcribed from the JACAR copies (no cipher groups were copied, so there is no cipher transcription); compared with FRUS in frus_pairs.md and gaps/. Bundles (1)-(8) only; bundles (9)-(16) are inventoried. Working notes in French.
texts.summary: US Navy Asiatic Fleet traffic and State Department telegrams on the Shanghai fighting, the League of Nations (Lytton) inquiry and Manchukuo, as read in Tokyo.

reading_review.note: Sample read: bundle 3 (C05022468000) images 01-02 and the comparison table frus_pairs.md. The copies are English telegrams with blanks and truncations, which read as sentences where the Japanese office recovered the words (rates 45-95 % by telegram, about 77 % on average per Brice Dudout's measure) and break at the unread passages; not read in full by the reviewer. Grade B: coherent but raw.

prior.where: the Japanese Navy's recovered clear texts themselves (the file)

human: Brice Dudout found the file among JACAR searches on Japanese intercepts, set the rules (statistical protocols written before calculation, batch d held out) and chose what to publish; AI agents inventoried, transcribed, compared with FRUS and wrote up.
